claim: even english splits into two physical standards: uk english uses the iso board with 102 keys, the extra key between left shift and z, and a shorter left shift, while us english uses the 101-key ansi board with horizontal return, so the v0.1 english version must ask which english rather than treat english as one keyboard.

source.title: UK vs US Keyboard Layout: Every Difference Explained

excerpt: ISO has 102 keys to ANSI’s 101. The extra one sits between the left Shift and the Z , which makes the left Shift noticeably shorter.
extracted: uk_english = ISO physical (102 keys, extra key at left shift, vertical enter); us_english = ANSI (101 keys, horizontal enter)

claim: azerty, the french and belgian logical standard, is three swaps from qwerty: a with q, z with w, and m moves from the bottom row to the semicolon key beside l, so a french buyer needs qwerty legends replaced, not just iso geometry.
excerpt: three letter changes define it: A and Q trade places, Z and W trade places, and M leaves QWERTY's bottom row to sit beside L, on the key where QWERTY puts the semicolon
extracted: azerty = qwerty with a<->q, z<->w, m on the semicolon key (fr/be logical layout)

claim: qwertz is the central-europe standard: the germany and austria pc layout is standardized on din 2137-2 and takes its name from z replacing y in the top-left six, so a german buyer differs from a us buyer in logical layout, physical key count, and legend set all at once.
excerpt: QWERTZUIOP keyboard is a typewriter and keyboard layout widely used in Central and Southeast Europe . The name comes from the first six letters at the top left of the keyboard The PC keyboard layout commonly used in Germany and Austria is based on one defined in a former edition (October 1988) of the German standard DIN 2137-2
extracted: qwertz = din 2137-2 based de/at layout, z replaces y in the top-left six

claim: the nordic family places the a-ring to the right of p to match the norwegian and swedish/finnish boards, but legend placements differ between the norwegian/danish and swedish/finnish pairs, so v0.4 nordic is two legend sets, not five.
excerpt: Å is to the right of P (to match the Norwegian and Swedish/Finnish keyboards)
extracted: nordic = Å right of P across no/se/fi boards, placements differ per language pair
